anchors.paper_title: Automatic sleep scoring for real-time monitoring and stimulation in individuals with and without sleep apnea
anchors.reason: Same group (Bitbrain, Sierra-Torralba, Klinzing) studies automatic sleep scoring CNNs using sleep datasets, but it is an algorithm study, not the BOAS data descriptor.

metadata.methods_description: Participants were recorded overnight with a Micromed PSG system (EEG, EOG, EMG, respiratory belts, thermistor, nasal cannula, PPG/SpO2) and simultaneously with a Bitbrain wearable headband (forehead EEG near AF7/AF8, IMU, PPG pulse). Three expert scorers independently staged PSG recordings per AASM criteria; consensus labels were taken by majority, with a fourth scorer resolving three-way disagreements. A deep learning model was trained with cross-validation on PSG and headband data to produce AI labels.

citation_details.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Self-Supervised Learning for Label-Efficient Sleep Staging with Wearable EEG
citation_details.author: Emilio Estevan, María Sierra-Torralba, Eduardo López‐Larraz, Luis Montesano
citation_details.abstract: Wearable EEG devices have emerged as a promising alternative to polysomnography (PSG). As affordable and scalable solutions, their widespread adoption results in the collection of massive volumes of unlabeled data that cannot be analyzed by clinicians at scale. Meanwhile, the recent success of deep learning for sleep scoring has relied on large annotated datasets. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers an opportunity to bridge this gap, leveraging unlabeled signals to address label scarcity and reduce annotation effort. citation_details.title: Trematodes of Genera Gyrabascus and Parabascus from Bats in European Russia: Morphology and Molecular Phylogeny
citation_details.author: Nadezhda Yu. Kirillova, Sergei V. Shchenkov, Alexander Kirillov, Alexander B. Ruchin
citation_details.abstract: Morphological variability of trematodes from bats (Chiroptera) is poorly studied. Since the variability of adult digenean specimens may be rather high, morphological features are often insufficient for the identification of closely related species, and confirmation with the use of molecular data is required. The aim of our study was to combine the morphological and molecular phylogenetic analyses of several bat trematodes from the genera Gyrabascus and Parabascus (Pleurogenidae): Gyrabascus amphoraeformis, Gyrabascus oppositus, Parabascus lepidotus, Parabascus duboisi, and Parabascus semisquamosus, of which G. amphoraeformis and G. oppositus are little known in European Russia. We made detailed morphological descriptions of these trematodes from several definitive hosts, analyzed morphometric features, and generated new partial sequences of the 28S rRNA gene. A broad variability of trematodes of the genera Gyrabascus and Parabascus was revealed both from various host species and from specimens of the same host species. We propose a new taxonomic key for the identification of the studied species. Certain host specificity of these trematodes was revealed.
